title: Investigate games with zero blunders detected
description:
8 out of 49 analyzed games (16%) had zero blunders detected by the Haiku pre-filter + Opus analysis pipeline. This seems suspicious given the current state of AI Magic play. The zero-blunder games are:

- game_20260214_123449_g4 (Standard, Haiku Villain vs MiMo Spike)
- game_20260214_123449_g5 (Standard, Gem3P Villain vs MiniMx Libby)
- game_20260214_155728_g1 (Modern, GPT4om Vorthos vs Llama4 Stoic)
- game_20260214_155728_g2 (Modern, Llama4 Timmy vs Qwen3L Stoic)
- game_20260214_165040_g5 (Standard, Gem3F Valley vs GPT4om Analyst)
- game_20260214_174030_g3 (Modern, Qwen3L Sarge vs Gem3F Coach)
- game_20260214_185313_g5 (Legacy, Kimi25 Libby vs MiMo Timmy)
- game_20260215_115110_g2 (Commander, Gem3F Coach vs GLM47/Qwen3L/KimiK2)

Possible causes:
1. Haiku pre-filter is too conservative and missing real blunders
2. Short/one-sided games where the winner played cleanly and the loser didn't get enough turns to blunder
3. Opus is dismissing flagged decisions too readily

Suggested investigation:
- Manually review a few zero-blunder games to spot blunders the pipeline missed
- Consider lowering the Haiku flagging threshold
- Consider having Opus review a random sample of unflagged decisions as a calibration check
